note: Terms this project withdrew, with what to say instead, and a ceiling on how many times each may still appear. A withdrawal recorded only in the glossary withdraws nothing: carrier was withdrawn on 2026-10-12 and used 173 times afterwards, including in work done two days later. The ceiling may be lowered freely and never raised, so the uses already written into dated records can stand -- they are evidence of what was thought at the time -- while a new use fails the build.

terms.insteadSay: prov:Entity for the value, port type for what a connection is checked against, or the class the value already asserts
terms.why: Defined as a prov:Entity that travels between ports, then withdrawn when no standard could be shown that defines such a class. The definition was derivable rather than new, and nothing consumed it.

classified.note: The classification direction `carrier-is-withdrawn-vocabulary` asked for and the count could not fall without: which occurrences are dated records that may not be reworded, and which are live text that should be. Measured by reading all of them, not by matching paths.

datedRecord.whyTheyStand: Experiment documents, dated audits and sweeps, widget and ruleset release files, and the lifted, narrowed and withdrawn entries in widgets/blockers.json. Each records what was thought on a date, and a withdrawn term inside one is the evidence. Rewording them would falsify the record.

files_: docs/audits/ontology-audit.md (the dated section that withdrew it)
recordsTheWithdrawal.whyTheyStand: These say the class is deliberately absent, or why a check lives elsewhere because it was rejected, or -- in src/old-naledi.ts -- that a sentence was reworded off the term. They cannot do that without naming it, for the same reason docs/glossary.md and this ledger are exempt. Not exempted here: an exemption would let new prose hide behind them, and these are few enough to read.

whereTheyWere: docs/audits/ontology-audit.md (D8a evidence, the D8 sweep count)
live.saidInstead: port type, where the text meant what a connection is checked against -- which was every case. `prov:Entity` and 'the class the value already asserts' were not needed.
